mechanism: Ritonavir inhibits CYP3A4 and CYP2C9, potentially increasing isoniazid levels and hepatotoxicity risk; isoniazid may induce CYP3A4, reducing ritonavir concentrations and antiretroviral efficacy.
action: Monitor liver function tests closely and consider isoniazid dose adjustment; ensure adequate ritonavir levels through therapeutic drug monitoring if available; assess for signs of isoniazid hepatotoxicity.
